briefing.headline: Two brand-new marketing reqs landed overnight — hit those before the stale prev-5/prev-6 pile you've already been ignoring.
briefing.focus: Spend the first 10 minutes on the fresh arrivals: Anthropic's Partner Marketing (Launches) posted yesterday and Datadog's Incident Response PMM posted 8/12 — both individual-contributor, both heavy H-1B sponsors. Then fire off the two remote-US anchors, Stripe's GTM PMM (your banking/fintech domain is a genuine edge there) and 6sense Partner Marketing (an ABM company reading an ABM resume). Close with CarGurus Boston — it's been on this list six days; either apply today or tell me to stop surfacing it.

ranked.why: Posted yesterday, zero prior pushes — partner launch marketing is exactly your positioning/messaging + enablement work, and Anthropic sponsors.
IC-level PMM at a major sponsor with a Boston engineering hub; incident response is a learnable domain and the req is only two days old.
Six years in banking/fintech makes you a domain hire, not a generalist applicant — and it's listed United States, not SF-only.
6sense IS an ABM platform; your ABM + funnel-metrics resume reads native here, and it's fully remote US.
The only real Boston B2B marketing role on the board and 'Specialist' means non-senior — six days of surfacing means apply or kill it.
The AMZ-numbered reqs are visa/PERM-tied postings — the single strongest sponsorship signal in today's list, and BA II is your analyst lane exactly.
'Audience & Messaging' is literally segmentation + positioning; keyword score of 88 badly under-rates a US-wide Figma PMM.
Remote-US and the rare role that pays for both lanes at once — GTM analytics with SQL and funnel metrics; five prior pushes is the only knock.
Radar is fraud/risk — you can speak to the buyer from six years inside banking, which almost no other PMM applicant can.
Remote-US marketing analyst, perfect on paper, but six straight recommendations with no action says you're avoiding it — decide.
ABX is ABM by another name; the 60 score is a scraping artifact from an empty JD, and Workday is a top-20 H-1B filer.
Fresh 8/13 req at a fast-growing infra company; growth marketing with real experimentation ownership.
GTM strategy and planning is the analytical side of your marketing lane; Gong is established enough to sponsor.
'Specialist' + B2B + performance marketing at Adobe is level-correct and sponsorship-safe; the 60 fit is an empty-JD artifact, not a real mismatch.
The cleanest marketing-analytics bridge role available — demand gen measurement at AWS — but six prior pushes means it's Seattle relocation you keep declining.
Lifecycle marketing at a product-analytics company suits an MBA in analytics; NYC hybrid, recent posting.
Analyst Relations is competitive-intelligence and positioning work in disguise — under-scored and nobody's pushed it before.
Remote GTM business ops at a public company (NYSE: IOT) — stable sponsor, and SQL/Salesforce carry the role.
Demand gen at a private-capital fintech — your channel-mix and pipeline work maps directly; five pushes though.
Marketing ops strategy is your Eloqua/HubSpot/attribution stack; SF-only is the friction, not the fit.
'Associate PMM' is precisely the non-senior level you want and the 69 score is nonsense for a positioning-heavy role.
Remote-US, specialist level, lifecycle + A/B testing — right level and right geography, low competition for someone with 6 years.
Remote-US demand gen program management; Grafana is past the risky-startup stage and the role is IC.
Boston-based business analyst at an established consumer-security company — geography is the whole argument; six pushes says you're lukewarm.
Literal ABM Manager at AWS — skill-perfect, but Arlington VA and five prior pushes with no move.
Never surfaced before; partner marketing built from scratch means broad scope, but SF-only and a young company.
Promotions analytics is the closest Amazon BA role to marketing measurement; Austin, and five prior pushes.
Boston + Klaviyo sponsors, but 'Product Owner, Sales Systems' is Salesforce administration, not marketing — a lane change, not a lateral.
Associate title fits the level and paid LinkedIn is squarely demand gen; five pushes suggests the NYC/SF requirement is the blocker.
Braze is a public MarTech company you'd sell credibly, but partner PMM is a narrower slice than your background.
Another visa-tied AMZ req, but BA III wants forecasting models and Python you don't have listed — a genuine stretch.
Remote-USA and crypto-fintech adjacency, but performance/paid media is the thinnest part of your resume.
Remote-US at Stripe is worth an application on sponsorship grounds alone, though GTM planning is more ops than marketing.
A 97 keyword score for a sales-ops analyst role with no Boston or remote option, pushed four times already — the score is inflated.
